findings.finding: Ardmore Shipping's Q3 release, published 3 November after Odfjell last spoke, has its IMO2 chemical tankers booked at about USD 30,100/day for 4Q26 at 60% fixed, against USD 23,266 earned in 3Q26 (+29%). Its MR product tankers are at USD 57,600 against USD 27,031. That points to a firmer 4Q26 guide from Odfjell than the 'reduced TCE ahead' it gave in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26 (2026-08-20): a strong quarter paired with a 'lower 3Q26' guide still moved +5.52%. 1Q26 (2026-05-06): an EPS miss against consensus (0.318 vs 0.417) moved -2.07%. 4Q25 (2026-02-11): -5.41%. The guide has not been isolated cleanly from the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It was published today, and ODF has fallen from 133.6 (5 Oct) to 119.6, 20d -8.3%. That is the opposite of a market positioned for a firmer Q4 chemical guide. ODF closed +1.5% on 3 November, which may be a partial read. It is a peer proxy: Ardmore's IMO2 25-38k dwt ships are swing tonnage, while Odfjell's core is stainless super-segregators with 46% COA cover, so transmission is partial. Odfjell itself names 'strong crude and product tanker earnings continue to limit swing tonnage' as the mechanism.
findings.independence: Kpler, 2026-10-06: a record 245 MRs trading dirty, 'Further ahead, we expect MR rates to firm' (https://www.kpler.com/blog/record-high-freight-as-risk-premiums-meet-tightening-fundamentals). That is the swing-tonnage channel Odfjell's own 2Q26 outlook names (https://newsweb.oslobors.no/message/680428).

findings.finding: Stolt-Nielsen, the closest deep-sea parcel-tanker peer, guided on 1 October that '4Q26 Stolt Tankers is expected to be slightly softer than 3Q26'. Norne's note adds that 'the chemical tanker market has captured only part of that momentum' from crude and product tankers. That argues against a firmer Odfjell Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: as above; Odfjell's reaction to its own guide changes has been 2-5.5% in either direction
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is five weeks old, from a widely read Oslo-listed peer, and the 10% drawdown since early October is consistent with it. It is sized small because Stolt's guide was set on Sep-Nov data before the October product-tanker acceleration Ardmore reports.
findings.independence: Stolt's own release, 2026-10-01: Q3 'stable versus the prior quarter, with firmer average freight rates offset by lower volumes and higher bunker costs' (https://www.inderes.dk/releases/stolt-nielsen-limited-reports-unaudited-results-for-the-third-quarter-and-nine-months-of-2026)

findings.finding: Peer Q3 prints bracket Odfjell's own 'closer to 1Q26' guide. Stolt's deep-sea TCE was USD 24,121/day in Jun-Aug against 23,372 in Mar-May (+3%). Ardmore's chemical spot was USD 23,266 in Q3 against 26,887 in Q2 (-13.5%). With Odfjell's commercial days up (two TC newbuilds in 2Q26, Bow Pluto in July), the quarter should land at or slightly above the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 1Q26 missed EPS consensus 0.318 vs 0.417 and moved -2.07%. 2Q26 was a strong quarter, +5.52%. 3Q25, 'in line with previous quarter', moved +2.87%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company told the market the quarter would be lower, and both peer prints are public. It is kept near zero because it lands inside the company's own guide. The only unpriced part is the fleet-days uplift.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance changes 9.0% against 2.3%) and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct 4.5 -> 5.0, because a shift from August's 'reduced TCE ahead' to a firmer 4Q26 guide would be a guidance change
